findings.title: NO email is queued — all send synchronously, blocking HTTP request
files: app/Mail/* (5 classes — NONE implements ShouldQueue, only `use Queueable` trait which is dormant without the interface)
findings.evidence: grep `ShouldQueue` over app/Mail returned only `VerifyEmail.php:6 use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue` — IMPORT line, but class declaration `class VerifyEmail extends Mailable` does NOT `implements ShouldQueue`. Dead import. grep `Mail::queue\|->onQueue` over app/Mail + app/Listeners/Send*Mail* returned ZERO matches. Every dispatch is `Mail::to(...)->send(...)`.
findings.impact: Production: customer clicks 'pay' → backend tries to send email → SMTP handshake to MAIL_HOST blocks the HTTP request for the duration of SMTP RTT (typically 200ms-5s depending on provider/network). On SMTP timeout (provider down, DNS issue, rate-limit), the HTTP request stalls or 500s. With QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis in production (.env.example:153 mandatory), the email SHOULD be queued and processed by `php artisan queue:work` daemon out-of-band. Currently it isn't.
findings.fix_recommended: Add `implements ShouldQueue` + `Illuminate\Bus\Queueable` (already trait-used) to all 5 Mail classes. Or change dispatch sites to `Mail::to($x)->queue(new OrderMail(...))`. With redis queue + worker daemon, emails flow into `emails` or `default` queue and HTTP returns immediately. Retry on failure becomes automatic via Laravel's queue tries config.

findings.title: Listener try/catch SWALLOWS Mail send failures — no retry, no alerting, no dead-letter
findings.evidence: Every Mail send is wrapped in `try { Mail::to(...)->send(...); } catch (\Exception $e) { Log::info($e->getMessage()); }`. `Log::info` (not `Log::error` / `Log::warning`) — passes below most alert thresholds. No retry, no dead-letter table, no escalation. SMTP transient failure (rate-limit, TLS handshake) → silent drop.
findings.impact: Password reset email lost → user can't login → silent breakage. Customer order confirmation lost → confused customer / refund request. Operator has no telemetry on email delivery success rate. Compounds with F-03 (sync send) because even if queue worker is added, the listener still catches and swallows the failure BEFORE Laravel's queue-retry kicks in.
findings.fix_recommended: (a) Remove try/catch from listeners — let exceptions propagate to Laravel queue handler which auto-retries with backoff. (b) If catch must stay (for sync send compatibility), use `Log::error()` + dispatch an alert event (`MailDeliveryFailedEvent` → email-channel-fallback / Slack webhook). (c) Add `dead_letter_emails` table (provider, recipient, subject, payload, last_error, attempts) for ops visibility. F-03 fix (ShouldQueue) is prerequisite for clean failure model.

findings.title: Production cutover BLOCKER — no email provider picked; defaults to hello@example.com

config/services.php:18-21 — Mailgun service config block present (`MAILGUN_DOMAIN`, `MAILGUN_SECRET`, `MAILGUN_ENDPOINT`) — half-wired, no driver active

No production boot guard exists for MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS or MAIL_USERNAME / MAIL_PASSWORD. Mailgun config block is in config/services.php but no API key, no domain bound, no smoke-test command. SPF / DKIM / DMARC records are DNS-side concerns owner must coordinate with domain registrar — not auditable from code.
findings.impact: Day-1 production: zero customer emails will land in inbox (SPF=fail, DMARC=reject). Password reset emails will silently drop. Branch admin order notifications will silently drop. Compounded with F-04 (failures swallowed), no telemetry surface signals the breakdown.
findings.fix_recommended: OWNER-GATE: pick provider. Recommended for V1 Le Cayenne single-resto: Mailgun (already half-wired, free tier ~5k mails/mo). Alternatives: SendGrid, Postmark, Brevo (FR-hosted, RGPD-friendly), Amazon SES (cheapest at scale but heavy ops). Once picked: (a) DNS: SPF TXT record (v=spf1 include:mailgun.org ~all) + DKIM CNAME + DMARC TXT (v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@lecayenne.example). (b) Add AppServiceProvider boot guard: refuse to boot in production if MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS contains 'example.com' or is empty — mirrors the existing MAIL_HOST SSRF guard (L7.2). (c) Smoke-test artisan command `php artisan mail:smoke noreply@lecayenne.example.com` that sends a probe + asserts SMTP 250.

findings.title: NO bounce / spam-complaint handling — bounces are silently dropped on provider side
files: app/Http/Controllers/* — no MailBounceController, no MailWebhookController grep matches
findings.evidence: No route, no controller, no listener for Mailgun/SendGrid bounce webhooks. Customer typos email → hard bounce → provider records it → app has no visibility, will keep trying to send to dead address. Eventually provider reputation degrades.
findings.impact: Sender reputation slowly poisoned by repeated bounces — provider may rate-limit or suspend account. No way to disable email for users who bounce repeatedly.
findings.fix_recommended: Add `bounced_emails` table + `MailWebhookController::handleBounce()` with provider signature verification. On hard bounce → flag `users.email_bounced_at`. Skip mail dispatch if flag set. Mailgun: webhook signing via timestamp+signature HMAC.

findings.title: PII over-share — emails include order_serial_no but lack RGPD data-minimization labelling / consent footer
findings.evidence: Customer-facing OrderMail body contains: customer name, order serial number, status message. Does NOT contain pricing details / item names — that's NOT in the email body, only an order ID reference. Data minimization is decent. HOWEVER: no unsubscribe link in any template (RGPD Article 21 right to object), no privacy-policy link, no `Pour cesser de recevoir ces emails, contactez...` footer.
findings.impact: RGPD Article 12-14 transparency requirement: every electronic comm must reference the data controller + give opt-out path. Article 21: right to object to direct marketing. Transactional emails have a narrower exemption (legitimate interest for service delivery) but contact info + opt-out for non-essential mails is best practice.
findings.fix_recommended: Add footer to mail layout: `Le Cayenne — <address>. Vous recevez cet email suite à votre commande #{order_id}. Pour gérer vos préférences, contactez nous@lecayenne.fr`. For NotificationAlert-keyed mails (non-essential): add unsubscribe link or per-status opt-out in user account.

findings.title: Locale NOT switched per recipient — emails always render in app current-request locale (which is FR for site default, but no per-user pref)
findings.evidence: Laravel Mailable supports `(new OrderMail($x))->locale($user->locale)` to render in recipient's language. NONE of the 4 dispatch paths use this. If `users` table grows a `locale` column (or already has one and code ignores it), emails render in the requesting agent's locale not the recipient's. For Le Cayenne V1 (FR-only customers), this is moot — but for SaaS V2 multi-tenant it's a P0.
findings.fix_recommended: Add `$mailable->locale($recipient->locale ?? config('app.locale'))` to every dispatch. Lock down to ['fr', 'en', 'ar'] allowlist matching app supported locales. V1 = nice-to-have; V2 SaaS = mandatory.

findings.title: NotificationAlert mail_message stored as varchar(255) — truncates long messages silently

findings.fix_recommended: Migrate column to TEXT. Or add MailRequest validator `'mail_message' => ['max:255']` and document the cap in admin UI tooltip.

verdict: PARTIAL — NOT V1 SHIP BLOCKER but PRODUCTION-CUTOVER BLOCKER on F-05
verdict_reasoning: Email subsystem is FUNCTIONAL for the narrow path it covers (admin gets new-order alert, customer with email gets status update IF operator flips switches ON), but has 5 P1 issues that collectively make it unsafe for production day-1: (1) F-01 + F-02 entire flow English on French site — brand damage + spam-filter signal — fixable with i18n keys + owner-gate French copy, (2) F-03 + F-04 sync send with swallowed errors — emails silently dropped on SMTP failure — fixable by adding ShouldQueue + removing try/catch swallow, (3) F-05 no provider picked + default MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=hello@example.com — emails will hard-bounce day-1 — REQUIRES OWNER-GATE PROVIDER DECISION + DNS coordination 24-48h before cutover. The 4 P2 findings (F-06 bounce handling, F-07 RGPD footer, F-08 locale switch, MISSING-03 refund email) are valuable hardening but not cutover blockers. The 3 P3 findings (F-09 varchar truncation, F-10 subject reuse, F-11 test infra) are polish. V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne can ship WITHOUT email cutover if owner accepts: (a) no customer email confirmations, (b) admin-side new-order alerts off (uses POS/KDS realtime instead), (c) password reset relies on PIN flow that owner verbally walks user through. The CURRENT default state (all 11 NotificationAlert switches OFF + no provider configured) is FAIL-CLOSED — no email is sent, no bounce, no damage — which is the right V1 posture pending provider decision. Going from FAIL-CLOSED to ACTIVE = F-05 owner-gate + F-01..F-04 hardening pass.
